_meta.indication: LIVMARLI is indicated for the treatment of cholestatic pruritus in patients with Alagille syndrome (ALGS) 1 year of age and older.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study LUM001-304 (the pivotal trial supporting approval)
pivotal_trials.design: Open-label run-in with a 4-week double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized withdrawal (RWD) period; the FDA focused on the 4-week RWD period comparing patients remaining on maralixibat with those switched to placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Pediatric patients with Alagille syndrome (ALGS) with elevated serum bile acid levels (>3x the upper limit of normal for age).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: The protocol-specified primary endpoint was mean change from Week 18 to 22 in fasting sBA level (in participants with sBA reduction >=50%); however sBA was not a validated surrogate, and effects on pruritus (ItchRO[Obs]) were secondary endpoints without a prespecified single primary pruritus endpoint, on which FDA based the efficacy conclusion.
pivotal_trials.n: 31 patients enrolled in the open-label run-in; 29 randomized to the RWD period (maralixibat 400 mcg/kg N=13; placebo N=16).
pivotal_trials.result: For the weekly average worst daily ItchRO(Obs) score, change from Week 18 to Week 22 was 0.2 (95% CI -0.3, 0.7) for maralixibat vs 1.6 (95% CI 1.2, 2.1) for placebo, mean treatment difference -1.4 (95% CI -2.1, -0.8), favoring continued maralixibat.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=5%) are diarrhea (55.8%), abdominal pain (53.5%), vomiting (40.7%), fat-soluble vitamin deficiency (25.6%), transaminases increased/liver test abnormalities (18.6%), gastrointestinal bleeding (10.4%), and bone fractures (9.3%).
target_moa: Maralixibat is an inhibitor of the ileal bile acid transporter (IBAT); ~95% of bile acids are reabsorbed in the terminal ileum, and IBAT inhibition reduces reabsorption of bile salts, lowering serum bile acid levels.
modality: Small molecule (molecular formula C40H56ClN3O5S; molecular weight 710.42 g/mol).

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held; the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues that were unexpected in the indicated population.

Maralixibat is an intestinal bile acid transport (IBAT) inhibitor that was granted Breakthrough Therapy designation for drug development as well as a Rare Pediatric Disease Designation for the treatment of pruritus associated with ALGS.

The Applicant was granted a rare pediatric disease designation from the Office of Orphan Products Development and the Office of Pediatric Therapeutics and met all criteria for receiving a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher.
